name: Quebec: Francisation Québec French courses for newcomers
name_fr: Québec : cours de français de Francisation Québec
description: Francisation Québec, created by Bill 96, is the single government access point for learning French. Courses are free for immigrants aged 16+ living in Quebec, including temporary workers, with financial assistance for full-time study.

attributes.eligibility_full_time_immigrants: Born outside Canada, 16 or older, living in Quebec; people planning to settle may also access services
attributes.temporary_residents: Temporary workers may register for full- or part-time courses; temporary students only if enrolled in a recognised programme as main occupation
attributes.cost: Free tuition and admission; small fees possible for materials or outings
attributes.format: Full-time sessions of 10 weeks at 25–30 hours per week; part-time and fully online options; free beginner platform francais-enligne.quebec
attributes.financial_assistance: Incentive assistance for full-time courses; none for individual part-time participants since 23 September 2024; none for fully online courses
attributes.obligation: No general legal obligation on individual newcomers to take courses was identified; French requirements arise through immigration selection (see nat-qc-skilled-worker-selection-program) and the six-month service rule (nat-qc-public-services-language).
attributes.status_dependency: Matters only if Quebec is in scope (USER-PROFILE.md: 'English-only vs bilingual environment' unknown) and depends on the user's status and French ability (unknown).
